parts.instruction: You will hear three different extracts. For questions 1-6, choose the answer (A, B or C) which fits best

questions.prompt: What do they like about the course most?

options.label: the way the course is delivered
the teacher’s attitude to the students
the content of the sessions

questions.prompt: According to the woman, how could the course be improved?

options.label: give assignment feedback
allow unlimited access to certain resources
give pre-course information for students

questions.prompt: What does he say about his luggage?

options.label: He’s hasn’t found the perfect bag yet.
He’s learnt to leave out unnecessary pieces of equipment.
He’s become very good at packing the absolute minimum.

questions.prompt: When asked what he’s learnt from travelling, he says that

options.label: he would now like to settle down somewhere.
he realises that his opportunity to travel is quite rare.
he feels bad about living in poor countries.

questions.prompt: How does he feel about the criticism of his band’s latest album cover?

options.label: He thinks it’s been exaggerated.
He admits it’s the reaction he was going for.
He resents the suggestion that the cover was unoriginal.

questions.prompt: He thinks much of the criticism was due to

options.label: a lack of respect for his band in the music business.
a foolish comment he made to a journalist.
a misunderstanding of his real intentions.

parts.instruction: You will hear a student called Kerry giving a class presentation about a type of bird called the swift.. For questions 7-14, complete the sentences.

questions.prompt: Kerry says that the Latin name for the swift translates to the words ________ in English.
Kerry describes the noise made by swifts as a ________.
Kerry says many people think that the bird’s shape most resembles a ________.
Kerry thinks that the swifts’ natural nesting site is on ________.
Kerry was surprised to learn that ________ is a common material found in swifts’ nests.
Kerry has observed swifts flying fast to avoid ________.
Kerry says that swifts tend to be strangely ________ when they are in Africa.
In the past, a rich family’s ________ often used the swift as a symbol.

parts.instruction: You will hear an interview in which two professional kayakers called Glenda Beachley and Declan Speight are talking about their sport.. For questions 15-20, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which fits best according to what you hear.

questions.prompt: What does Glenda find most enjoyable about kayaking?

options.label: It needs a variety of skills.
It puts your fitness to the test.
It requires her to work out problems.
It makes her feel more independent.

questions.prompt: Glenda suggests that amateur kayakers should

options.label: alter different training techniques.
take picking a club seriously.
focus on the fun the sport gives.
be as competitive with friends as possible.

questions.prompt: When Declan brings up ‘wild-water’ racing, he suggests that

options.label: it tests your endurance rather than speed.
keeping to the given route can be tricky.
weather is the main factor determining his success.
competitions are the main motivation for him.

questions.prompt: When asked about the possible dangers, Glenda believes that

options.label: a degree of danger makes the sport interesting.
you’ve got to learn from your mistakes.
good risk-assessing skill is a must.
being too confident is especially dangerous.

questions.prompt: What does Declan recommend when buying equipment?

options.label: Investing in the best equipment you can afford.
Asking help of a more experienced person.
Getting what is most comfortable for you.
Researching before making a purchase.

questions.prompt: Both Glenda’s and Declan’s best memories of kayaking are connected with

options.label: going to new locations with people they know well.
showing good results in competitions.
meeting various people.
finding great kayaking spots in unexpected places.
